best_for: ClauseCrosswalk sets a table of requirements against two regulations' clauses as an editorial crosswalk: the requirements large down the middle, each regulation a spine at the outer edge with its name set big and vertical and its clauses as chips, and a wire from every requirement to every clause it cites.

block.h: Which water each standard asks for
block.intro: None of these is Purified Water. Purified Water is held to ≤ 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C (USP <645> stage 1), with no endotoxin limit.
cols: How it differs from Purified Water
rows: Fewer ions removed, far tighter on microbes, plus an endotoxin limit: < 10 µS/cm, < 10 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL, < 10 endotoxin units/mL
Looser: < 500 µS/cm, < 500 CFU/mL. As the final rinse after high-level disinfection: < 10 CFU/mL and < 10 endotoxin units/mL
Tighter on ions and organic carbon: < 1 µS/cm at 25 °C, total organic carbon < 50 µg/L
Tighter on ions than Type II, looser on organic carbon: < 0.25 µS/cm at 25 °C, total organic carbon < 200 µg/L. Not a purity ladder
Defined for medical laboratories; an analyzer maker's specification governs that analyzer's feed
Made at the bench by a point-of-use polisher fed from the loop, not by a central loop
